o:
We need FIFO queues for waiting riders and available drivers, plus a way to ignore riders who cancelled before being matched. Matching pops the front of both queues. Because ids are added at most once and calls are ≤ 1000, even simple structures suffice.

Example 1: riders [3,1], drivers [2]; match → (2,3); driver 5 arrives; cancelling rider 3 is a no-op (already matched); match → (5,1); then nothing remains → [-1,-1]. Example 2 shows cancellation of a still-waiting rider: rider 2 is skipped, so the next match finds nothing.
k: Lazy deletion: mark cancelled ids and skip them when they reach the queue front.

a.n: Approach 1: Two FIFO queues with lazy cancellation
a.i: Keep a deque of riders and a deque of drivers in arrival order. On match, pop any cancelled riders from the rider front first; if both queues are non-empty, pop one from each. Cancelled riders buried mid-queue are harmless because they are discarded when they surface.
s: addRider/addDriver append to the respective deque.
cancelRider adds the id to a cancelled set (no queue scan needed).
matchDriverWithRider: while rider front is cancelled, pop it; if either queue is empty return [-1,-1]; otherwise pop both fronts and return [driverId, riderId].
a.t: O(1) amortized per operation — each rider is popped from the queue at most once
a.sp: O(n) — queues and the cancellation set

a.n: Approach 2: Linked-list style skip via status map
a.i: Store every rider/driver in insertion-order lists together with a status map (waiting/matched/cancelled). Matching advances a shared pointer over the rider list, skipping non-waiting entries. This makes cancelRider an O(1) status flip and avoids ever removing from the middle of a structure.
s: Keep arrays riderOrder/driverOrder and status maps.
advance pointers past non-waiting entries during match.
cancelRider sets status to cancelled if currently waiting.
a.t: O(1) amortized per call — pointers only move forward
a.sp: O(n) — order lists and status maps

w: Both approaches are equivalent asymptotically; the deque + cancelled-set version is the most idiomatic. Pitfalls: eagerly removing a cancelled rider from the middle of the queue (unnecessary O(n)), and forgetting that cancelling an already-matched rider must be a no-op. Follow-up: support driver cancellation, or match nearest driver instead of earliest (requires ordered structures by location).
